critique.strongest_angle: Connecting XRP's 16% price expansion and $487M volume directly to the verified shift in time-of-day on-chain activity, while framing institutional involvement as an analytical hypothesis rather than a fact.
weak_points: Claiming 'bankers are buying' would be an overreach; Western trading hours also coincide with active US crypto funds and automated market makers.

draft.title: XRP Rallies 16% to $1.29: What the 'Banker Hours' Data Really Reveals
draft.post:
Almost a quarter of all XRP on-chain movement now happens during a tight three-hour window between London and New York financial hours.

As XRP surged 16.2% over 24 hours to touch $1.295, Binance spot volumes crossed $487 million USDT—making it one of the most heavily traded assets on the exchange.

On-chain data published by CoinDesk highlights a noticeable shift: transactions during the London afternoon and New York morning overlap now account for roughly 23% of XRP's daily on-chain volume, up from about 14% a year ago.

While high activity during Western working hours points to structured liquidity flows rather than random weekend retail spikes, price action shows volatility remains two-sided. During the peak of the move, a single 1-hour candle processed over 43 million XRP, pulling price back to $1.228 before buyers stepped in to absorb the sell-off.

The key question now is whether this time-of-day liquidity concentration represents long-term institutional accumulation or simply active algorithmic trading capitalizing on volatility.

What to watch next: How XRP holds the $1.22–$1.25 retest zone as European and US markets open for the next session.

Follow for evidence-based market breakdowns and real-time data analysis.
